TSC members, as well as nominate additional reviewers.

Contributors who are removed from the list for large scopes:
the proposal makes a loose assumption that they are no longer actively
developing and/or reviewing the affected segments of the codebase. Thus,
the PR should only go in once it satisfies edit requests and a general
approval by such long-standing contributors and code owners.

thereof to higher-level code owners.
Any contributor, regardless of TSC membership, is generally free to
volunteer for the existing or narrower review scopes, as well as
offload notifications and first-point-of-contact duties to other
project members.

commit_message:
Fix inline HAL storage buffer leak on release

iree_vm_buffer_destroy assumed every non-module-owned buffer was
co-allocated with its data by iree_vm_buffer_create, and therefore
freed the handle with iree_allocator_free_aligned. This is invalid for
buffers initialized in-place over caller-owned storage, such as the
inline HAL storage buffer wrapper, and caused the wrapper to leak in the
inline execution model end-to-end test.

Hence, tag buffers created/cloned with
IREE_VM_BUFFER_ACCESS_COALLOCATED and only use the aligned free path
for those. Other buffers pass the handle directly to their allocator.

Also initialize the inline storage buffer's host_allocator and
hal_buffer fields. Without this, destroying the wrapper would use a
null allocator and fail to release the retained HAL buffer.

Assisted-by: Claude Code
Signed-off-by: Pooja Hemashekar <hemashekar@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for pack

Extends distribution inner-tile alignment hints to pack ops. A scalable pack's
distribution tile is now aligned to base * vscaleMax, so it is a whole multiple
of the runtime inner tile and gets a `distribution` hint of `Multiple`. This
covers both a pack tiled directly and a pack that consumes an unpack
(`annotateScalablePackConsumerOfUnpack`), which derives its distribution hint
from the unpack's distribution tiles: a match only yields `Multiple` when the
distribution tile is a whole multiple of the pack's largest inner tile, so a
pack whose scalable inner tile differs from its unpack producer's gets no hint.

Packs whose scalable dim is not distributed (e.g. a reduction/broadcast pack)
and mmt4d-fused packs (which distribute on outer dims) are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[Codegen] Forward distribution inner-tile alignment hints in forall tiling

Threads the distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints (set on scalable
`linalg.pack`/`linalg.unpack` ops during lowering-strategy selection) into
`TileAndDistributeToWorkgroupsUsingForall`, via
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn(DistributionTiles)` on both the tiling options and the
consumer-fusion step. With a `Multiple` hint the workgroup tiling folds a
scalable/dynamic inner tile to a clean `tile ceildiv innerTile` division instead
of leaving the pack/unpack untiled.

Adds lit coverage: two scalable pack/unpack cases (hint forwarded and preserved
through tiling) and a dynamic-inner-tile case where the hint is load-bearing —
the pack is only tiled into the forall because the hint asserts the multiple
relationship the driver cannot infer from the IR.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Align scalable distribution tiles to base * vscaleMax

Distribution tiles for scalable pack/unpack inner dims are aligned to the
largest possible inner tile (`base * vscaleMax`) instead of the static base,
so the per-workgroup inner shape stays static for any runtime vscale. This
updates the four sites that align distribution to inner tiles:

- root unpack (`setRootConfig(UnPackOp)`),
- root pack (`setRootConfig(PackOp)`), which previously opted out entirely for
  its element-wise behavior but must still align *scalable* dims,
- a non-root pack fused into a root (`adjustTileSizesForRootOp`),
- a root op fusing an unpack (`adjustTileSizesForRootUnPackOp`).

Non-scalable dims and mmt4d/matmul (which distribute on outer dims) are
unchanged. When no `vscale_range` is available the previous static-base +
round-up-to-pow2 behavior is kept.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>
name: pre-commit

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Add vscale_range target field, require it for scalable vec

Add a user-specifiable vscale_range that is recorded on the executable target. This will be used for lowering later on, specifically while setting tile sizes and aligning them to scalable vector sizes.

For targets that support scalable vectorization, specifying this flag is a requirement if scalable vectorization is also enabled. If the target has +zvl*b features and the user specifies a lower bound, the maximum of the two lower bounds will be effective.

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for pack

Extends distribution inner-tile alignment hints to pack ops. A scalable pack's
distribution tile is now aligned to base * vscaleMax, so it is a whole multiple
of the runtime inner tile and gets a `distribution` hint of `Multiple`. This
covers both a pack tiled directly and a pack that consumes an unpack
(`annotateScalablePackConsumerOfUnpack`), which derives its distribution hint
from the unpack's distribution tiles: a match only yields `Multiple` when the
distribution tile is a whole multiple of the pack's largest inner tile, so a
pack whose scalable inner tile differs from its unpack producer's gets no hint.

Packs whose scalable dim is not distributed (e.g. a reduction/broadcast pack)
and mmt4d-fused packs (which distribute on outer dims) are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for unpack

After distribution tiles are aligned to base * vscaleMax (see the preceding
change), a scalable unpack's distribution tile is a whole multiple of the
runtime inner tile for any vscale, so record a `distribution` inner-tile
alignment hint of `Multiple` on it.

A distribution tile is classified as `Multiple` only when it is a whole
multiple of the largest inner tile; mmt4d-fused unpacks (which distribute on
outer dims and are not aligned to inner tiles) therefore get no distribution
hint. Pack distribution hints are added separately.

commit_message:
[Codegen] Forward distribution inner-tile alignment hints in forall tiling

Threads the distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints (set on scalable
`linalg.pack`/`linalg.unpack` ops during lowering-strategy selection) into
`TileAndDistributeToWorkgroupsUsingForall`, via
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn(DistributionTiles)` on both the tiling options and the
consumer-fusion step. With a `Multiple` hint the workgroup tiling folds a
scalable/dynamic inner tile to a clean `tile ceildiv innerTile` division instead
of leaving the pack/unpack untiled.

Adds lit coverage: two scalable pack/unpack cases (hint forwarded and preserved
through tiling) and a dynamic-inner-tile case where the hint is load-bearing —
the pack is only tiled into the forall because the hint asserts the multiple
relationship the driver cannot infer from the IR.

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Align scalable distribution tiles to base * vscaleMax

Distribution tiles for scalable pack/unpack inner dims are aligned to the
largest possible inner tile (`base * vscaleMax`) instead of the static base,
so the per-workgroup inner shape stays static for any runtime vscale. This
updates the four sites that align distribution to inner tiles:

- root unpack (`setRootConfig(UnPackOp)`),
- root pack (`setRootConfig(PackOp)`), which previously opted out entirely for
  its element-wise behavior but must still align *scalable* dims,
- a non-root pack fused into a root (`adjustTileSizesForRootOp`),
- a root op fusing an unpack (`adjustTileSizesForRootUnPackOp`).

Non-scalable dims and mmt4d/matmul (which distribute on outer dims) are
unchanged. When no `vscale_range` is available the previous static-base +
round-up-to-pow2 behavior is kept.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for pack

Extends distribution inner-tile alignment hints to pack ops. A scalable pack's
distribution tile is now aligned to base * vscaleMax, so it is a whole multiple
of the runtime inner tile and gets a `distribution` hint of `Multiple`. This
covers both a pack tiled directly and a pack that consumes an unpack
(`annotateScalablePackConsumerOfUnpack`), which derives its distribution hint
from the unpack's distribution tiles: a match only yields `Multiple` when the
distribution tile is a whole multiple of the pack's largest inner tile, so a
pack whose scalable inner tile differs from its unpack producer's gets no hint.

Packs whose scalable dim is not distributed (e.g. a reduction/broadcast pack)
and mmt4d-fused packs (which distribute on outer dims) are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Add vscale_range target field, require it for scalable vec

Add a user-specifiable vscale_range that is recorded on the executable target. This will be used for lowering later on, specifically while setting tile sizes and aligning them to scalable vector sizes.

For targets that support scalable vectorization, specifying this flag is a requirement if scalable vectorization is also enabled. If the target has +zvl*b features and the user specifies a lower bound, the maximum of the two lower bounds will be effective.

Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

For targets that support scalable vectorization, specifying this flag is a requirement if scalable vectorization is also enabled. If the target has +zvl*b features and the user specifies a lower bound, the maximum of the two lower bounds will be effective.

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for unpack

After distribution tiles are aligned to base * vscaleMax (see the preceding
change), a scalable unpack's distribution tile is a whole multiple of the
runtime inner tile for any vscale, so record a `distribution` inner-tile
alignment hint of `Multiple` on it.

A distribution tile is classified as `Multiple` only when it is a whole
multiple of the largest inner tile; mmt4d-fused unpacks (which distribute on
outer dims and are not aligned to inner tiles) therefore get no distribution
hint. Pack distribution hints are added separately.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>
name: setup / setup

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for unpack

After distribution tiles are aligned to base * vscaleMax (see the preceding
change), a scalable unpack's distribution tile is a whole multiple of the
runtime inner tile for any vscale, so record a `distribution` inner-tile
alignment hint of `Multiple` on it.

A distribution tile is classified as `Multiple` only when it is a whole
multiple of the largest inner tile; mmt4d-fused unpacks (which distribute on
outer dims and are not aligned to inner tiles) therefore get no distribution
hint. Pack distribution hints are added separately.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Align scalable distribution tiles to base * vscaleMax

Distribution tiles for scalable pack/unpack inner dims are aligned to the
largest possible inner tile (`base * vscaleMax`) instead of the static base,
so the per-workgroup inner shape stays static for any runtime vscale. This
updates the four sites that align distribution to inner tiles:

- root unpack (`setRootConfig(UnPackOp)`),
- root pack (`setRootConfig(PackOp)`), which previously opted out entirely for
  its element-wise behavior but must still align *scalable* dims,
- a non-root pack fused into a root (`adjustTileSizesForRootOp`),
- a root op fusing an unpack (`adjustTileSizesForRootUnPackOp`).

Non-scalable dims and mmt4d/matmul (which distribute on outer dims) are
unchanged. When no `vscale_range` is available the previous static-base +
round-up-to-pow2 behavior is kept.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Align scalable distribution tiles to base * vscaleMax

Distribution tiles for scalable pack/unpack inner dims are aligned to the
largest possible inner tile (`base * vscaleMax`) instead of the static base,
so the per-workgroup inner shape stays static for any runtime vscale. This
updates the four sites that align distribution to inner tiles:

- root unpack (`setRootConfig(UnPackOp)`),
- root pack (`setRootConfig(PackOp)`), which previously opted out entirely for
  its element-wise behavior but must still align *scalable* dims,
- a non-root pack fused into a root (`adjustTileSizesForRootOp`),
- a root op fusing an unpack (`adjustTileSizesForRootUnPackOp`).

Non-scalable dims and mmt4d/matmul (which distribute on outer dims) are
unchanged. When no `vscale_range` is available the previous static-base +
round-up-to-pow2 behavior is kept.

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Add vscale_range target field, require it for scalable vec

Add a user-specifiable vscale_range that is recorded on the executable target. This will be used for lowering later on, specifically while setting tile sizes and aligning them to scalable vector sizes.

For targets that support scalable vectorization, specifying this flag is a requirement if scalable vectorization is also enabled. If the target has +zvl*b features and the user specifies a lower bound, the maximum of the two lower bounds will be effective.

Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

[LLVMCPU] Align scalable distribution tiles to base * vscaleMax

Distribution tiles for scalable pack/unpack inner dims are aligned to the
largest possible inner tile (`base * vscaleMax`) instead of the static base,
so the per-workgroup inner shape stays static for any runtime vscale. This
updates the four sites that align distribution to inner tiles:

- root unpack (`setRootConfig(UnPackOp)`),
- root pack (`setRootConfig(PackOp)`), which previously opted out entirely for
  its element-wise behavior but must still align *scalable* dims,
- a non-root pack fused into a root (`adjustTileSizesForRootOp`),
- a root op fusing an unpack (`adjustTileSizesForRootUnPackOp`).

Non-scalable dims and mmt4d/matmul (which distribute on outer dims) are
unchanged. When no `vscale_range` is available the previous static-base +
round-up-to-pow2 behavior is kept.

commit_message:
[Codegen] Forward distribution inner-tile alignment hints in forall tiling

Threads the distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints (set on scalable
`linalg.pack`/`linalg.unpack` ops during lowering-strategy selection) into
`TileAndDistributeToWorkgroupsUsingForall`, via
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn(DistributionTiles)` on both the tiling options and the
consumer-fusion step. With a `Multiple` hint the workgroup tiling folds a
scalable/dynamic inner tile to a clean `tile ceildiv innerTile` division instead
of leaving the pack/unpack untiled.

Adds lit coverage: two scalable pack/unpack cases (hint forwarded and preserved
through tiling) and a dynamic-inner-tile case where the hint is load-bearing —
the pack is only tiled into the forall because the hint asserts the multiple
relationship the driver cannot infer from the IR.

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for pack

Extends distribution inner-tile alignment hints to pack ops. A scalable pack's
distribution tile is now aligned to base * vscaleMax, so it is a whole multiple
of the runtime inner tile and gets a `distribution` hint of `Multiple`. This
covers both a pack tiled directly and a pack that consumes an unpack
(`annotateScalablePackConsumerOfUnpack`), which derives its distribution hint
from the unpack's distribution tiles: a match only yields `Multiple` when the
distribution tile is a whole multiple of the pack's largest inner tile, so a
pack whose scalable inner tile differs from its unpack producer's gets no hint.

Packs whose scalable dim is not distributed (e.g. a reduction/broadcast pack)
and mmt4d-fused packs (which distribute on outer dims) are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Align scalable distribution tiles to base * vscaleMax

Distribution tiles for scalable pack/unpack inner dims are aligned to the
largest possible inner tile (`base * vscaleMax`) instead of the static base,
so the per-workgroup inner shape stays static for any runtime vscale. This
updates the four sites that align distribution to inner tiles:

- root unpack (`setRootConfig(UnPackOp)`),
- root pack (`setRootConfig(PackOp)`), which previously opted out entirely for
  its element-wise behavior but must still align *scalable* dims,
- a non-root pack fused into a root (`adjustTileSizesForRootOp`),
- a root op fusing an unpack (`adjustTileSizesForRootUnPackOp`).

Non-scalable dims and mmt4d/matmul (which distribute on outer dims) are
unchanged. When no `vscale_range` is available the previous static-base +
round-up-to-pow2 behavior is kept.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[Codegen] Forward distribution inner-tile alignment hints in forall tiling

Threads the distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints (set on scalable
`linalg.pack`/`linalg.unpack` ops during lowering-strategy selection) into
`TileAndDistributeToWorkgroupsUsingForall`, via
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn(DistributionTiles)` on both the tiling options and the
consumer-fusion step. With a `Multiple` hint the workgroup tiling folds a
scalable/dynamic inner tile to a clean `tile ceildiv innerTile` division instead
of leaving the pack/unpack untiled.

Adds lit coverage: two scalable pack/unpack cases (hint forwarded and preserved
through tiling) and a dynamic-inner-tile case where the hint is load-bearing —
the pack is only tiled into the forall because the hint asserts the multiple
relationship the driver cannot infer from the IR.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for unpack

After distribution tiles are aligned to base * vscaleMax (see the preceding
change), a scalable unpack's distribution tile is a whole multiple of the
runtime inner tile for any vscale, so record a `distribution` inner-tile
alignment hint of `Multiple` on it.

A distribution tile is classified as `Multiple` only when it is a whole
multiple of the largest inner tile; mmt4d-fused unpacks (which distribute on
outer dims and are not aligned to inner tiles) therefore get no distribution
hint. Pack distribution hints are added separately.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[Codegen] Forward distribution inner-tile alignment hints in forall tiling

Threads the distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints (set on scalable
`linalg.pack`/`linalg.unpack` ops during lowering-strategy selection) into
`TileAndDistributeToWorkgroupsUsingForall`, via
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn(DistributionTiles)` on both the tiling options and the
consumer-fusion step. With a `Multiple` hint the workgroup tiling folds a
scalable/dynamic inner tile to a clean `tile ceildiv innerTile` division instead
of leaving the pack/unpack untiled.

Adds lit coverage: two scalable pack/unpack cases (hint forwarded and preserved
through tiling) and a dynamic-inner-tile case where the hint is load-bearing —
the pack is only tiled into the forall because the hint asserts the multiple
relationship the driver cannot infer from the IR.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>
name: clang-tidy

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for pack

Extends distribution inner-tile alignment hints to pack ops. A scalable pack's
distribution tile is now aligned to base * vscaleMax, so it is a whole multiple
of the runtime inner tile and gets a `distribution` hint of `Multiple`. This
covers both a pack tiled directly and a pack that consumes an unpack
(`annotateScalablePackConsumerOfUnpack`), which derives its distribution hint
from the unpack's distribution tiles: a match only yields `Multiple` when the
distribution tile is a whole multiple of the pack's largest inner tile, so a
pack whose scalable inner tile differs from its unpack producer's gets no hint.

Packs whose scalable dim is not distributed (e.g. a reduction/broadcast pack)
and mmt4d-fused packs (which distribute on outer dims) are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>
name: clang-tidy

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Align scalable distribution tiles to base * vscaleMax

Distribution tiles for scalable pack/unpack inner dims are aligned to the
largest possible inner tile (`base * vscaleMax`) instead of the static base,
so the per-workgroup inner shape stays static for any runtime vscale. This
updates the four sites that align distribution to inner tiles:

- root unpack (`setRootConfig(UnPackOp)`),
- root pack (`setRootConfig(PackOp)`), which previously opted out entirely for
  its element-wise behavior but must still align *scalable* dims,
- a non-root pack fused into a root (`adjustTileSizesForRootOp`),
- a root op fusing an unpack (`adjustTileSizesForRootUnPackOp`).

Non-scalable dims and mmt4d/matmul (which distribute on outer dims) are
unchanged. When no `vscale_range` is available the previous static-base +
round-up-to-pow2 behavior is kept.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>
name: clang-tidy

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Add vscale_range target field, require it for scalable vec

Add a user-specifiable vscale_range that is recorded on the executable target. This will be used for lowering later on, specifically while setting tile sizes and aligning them to scalable vector sizes.

For targets that support scalable vectorization, specifying this flag is a requirement if scalable vectorization is also enabled. If the target has +zvl*b features and the user specifies a lower bound, the maximum of the two lower bounds will be effective.

Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>
name: pre-commit

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Add vscale_range target field, require it for scalable vec

Add a user-specifiable vscale_range that is recorded on the executable target. This will be used for lowering later on, specifically while setting tile sizes and aligning them to scalable vector sizes.

For targets that support scalable vectorization, specifying this flag is a requirement if scalable vectorization is also enabled. If the target has +zvl*b features and the user specifies a lower bound, the maximum of the two lower bounds will be effective.

Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>
name: setup / setup

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for pack

Extends distribution inner-tile alignment hints to pack ops. A scalable pack's
distribution tile is now aligned to base * vscaleMax, so it is a whole multiple
of the runtime inner tile and gets a `distribution` hint of `Multiple`. This
covers both a pack tiled directly and a pack that consumes an unpack
(`annotateScalablePackConsumerOfUnpack`), which derives its distribution hint
from the unpack's distribution tiles: a match only yields `Multiple` when the
distribution tile is a whole multiple of the pack's largest inner tile, so a
pack whose scalable inner tile differs from its unpack producer's gets no hint.

Packs whose scalable dim is not distributed (e.g. a reduction/broadcast pack)
and mmt4d-fused packs (which distribute on outer dims) are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>
name: setup / setup

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for pack

Extends distribution inner-tile alignment hints to pack ops. A scalable pack's
distribution tile is now aligned to base * vscaleMax, so it is a whole multiple
of the runtime inner tile and gets a `distribution` hint of `Multiple`. This
covers both a pack tiled directly and a pack that consumes an unpack
(`annotateScalablePackConsumerOfUnpack`), which derives its distribution hint
from the unpack's distribution tiles: a match only yields `Multiple` when the
distribution tile is a whole multiple of the pack's largest inner tile, so a
pack whose scalable inner tile differs from its unpack producer's gets no hint.

Packs whose scalable dim is not distributed (e.g. a reduction/broadcast pack)
and mmt4d-fused packs (which distribute on outer dims) are unchanged.

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Add vscale_range target field, require it for scalable vec

Add a user-specifiable vscale_range that is recorded on the executable target. This will be used for lowering later on, specifically while setting tile sizes and aligning them to scalable vector sizes.

For targets that support scalable vectorization, specifying this flag is a requirement if scalable vectorization is also enabled. If the target has +zvl*b features and the user specifies a lower bound, the maximum of the two lower bounds will be effective.

Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>
name: setup / setup

[LLVMCPU] Add vscale_range target field, require it for scalable vec

Add a user-specifiable vscale_range that is recorded on the executable target. This will be used for lowering later on, specifically while setting tile sizes and aligning them to scalable vector sizes.

For targets that support scalable vectorization, specifying this flag is a requirement if scalable vectorization is also enabled. If the target has +zvl*b features and the user specifies a lower bound, the maximum of the two lower bounds will be effective.

Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>
name: runtime_small

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Align scalable distribution tiles to base * vscaleMax

Distribution tiles for scalable pack/unpack inner dims are aligned to the
largest possible inner tile (`base * vscaleMax`) instead of the static base,
so the per-workgroup inner shape stays static for any runtime vscale. This
updates the four sites that align distribution to inner tiles:

- root unpack (`setRootConfig(UnPackOp)`),
- root pack (`setRootConfig(PackOp)`), which previously opted out entirely for
  its element-wise behavior but must still align *scalable* dims,
- a non-root pack fused into a root (`adjustTileSizesForRootOp`),
- a root op fusing an unpack (`adjustTileSizesForRootUnPackOp`).

Non-scalable dims and mmt4d/matmul (which distribute on outer dims) are
unchanged. When no `vscale_range` is available the previous static-base +
round-up-to-pow2 behavior is kept.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>
name: setup / setup

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for pack

Extends distribution inner-tile alignment hints to pack ops. A scalable pack's
distribution tile is now aligned to base * vscaleMax, so it is a whole multiple
of the runtime inner tile and gets a `distribution` hint of `Multiple`. This
covers both a pack tiled directly and a pack that consumes an unpack
(`annotateScalablePackConsumerOfUnpack`), which derives its distribution hint
from the unpack's distribution tiles: a match only yields `Multiple` when the
distribution tile is a whole multiple of the pack's largest inner tile, so a
pack whose scalable inner tile differs from its unpack producer's gets no hint.

Packs whose scalable dim is not distributed (e.g. a reduction/broadcast pack)
and mmt4d-fused packs (which distribute on outer dims) are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[Codegen] Forward distribution inner-tile alignment hints in forall tiling

Threads the distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints (set on scalable
`linalg.pack`/`linalg.unpack` ops during lowering-strategy selection) into
`TileAndDistributeToWorkgroupsUsingForall`, via
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn(DistributionTiles)` on both the tiling options and the
consumer-fusion step. With a `Multiple` hint the workgroup tiling folds a
scalable/dynamic inner tile to a clean `tile ceildiv innerTile` division instead
of leaving the pack/unpack untiled.

Adds lit coverage: two scalable pack/unpack cases (hint forwarded and preserved
through tiling) and a dynamic-inner-tile case where the hint is load-bearing —
the pack is only tiled into the forall because the hint asserts the multiple
relationship the driver cannot infer from the IR.

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Add vscale_range target field, require it for scalable vec

Introduce a scalable-vector range (`vscale_range`, in vscale units), specified
via `--iree-llvmcpu-vscale-range=<max>` or `=<min,max>`. It is recorded on
`#hal.executable.target` as `vscale_range = [min, max]`.

`getVscaleRange` returns the effective range for a target: a user-specified
range on the config if present, otherwise the target's default
(`getDefaultVscaleRange`, still `{1, 16}` for AArch64 SVE), or nullopt if
neither exists. The LLVM `vscale_range` function attribute is stamped from the
range during serialization (a `+zvlNb` feature raises the min); both the
AArch64 (SVE) and RISC-V (RVV) backends consume it.

A scalable-capable target (SVE or `+v`) with scalable vectorization enabled must
resolve to some range, so strategy selection errors when neither a default nor a
user-specified range exists (e.g. RISC-V `+v` without --iree-llvmcpu-vscale-range).

Existing scalable tests record the range as `[1, 16]`; adds a round-trip test
and an enforcement test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Add vscale_range target field, require it for scalable vec

Introduce a scalable-vector range (`vscale_range`, in vscale units), specified
via `--iree-llvmcpu-vscale-range=<max>` or `=<min,max>`. It is recorded on
`#hal.executable.target` as `vscale_range = [min, max]`.

`getVscaleRange` returns the effective range for a target: a user-specified
range on the config if present, otherwise the target's default
(`getDefaultVscaleRange`, still `{1, 16}` for AArch64 SVE), or nullopt if
neither exists. The LLVM `vscale_range` function attribute is stamped from the
range during serialization (a `+zvlNb` feature raises the min); both the
AArch64 (SVE) and RISC-V (RVV) backends consume it.

A scalable-capable target (SVE or `+v`) with scalable vectorization enabled must
resolve to some range, so strategy selection errors when neither a default nor a
user-specified range exists (e.g. RISC-V `+v` without --iree-llvmcpu-vscale-range).

Existing scalable tests record the range as `[1, 16]`; adds a round-trip test
and an enforcement test.

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Align scalable distribution tiles to base * vscaleMax

Distribution tiles for scalable pack/unpack inner dims are aligned to the
largest possible inner tile (`base * vscaleMax`) instead of the static base,
so the per-workgroup inner shape stays static for any runtime vscale. This
updates the four sites that align distribution to inner tiles:

- root unpack (`setRootConfig(UnPackOp)`),
- root pack (`setRootConfig(PackOp)`), which previously opted out entirely for
  its element-wise behavior but must still align *scalable* dims,
- a non-root pack fused into a root (`adjustTileSizesForRootOp`),
- a root op fusing an unpack (`adjustTileSizesForRootUnPackOp`).

Non-scalable dims and mmt4d/matmul (which distribute on outer dims) are
unchanged. When no `vscale_range` is available the previous static-base +
round-up-to-pow2 behavior is kept.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

largest possible inner tile (`base * vscaleMax`) instead of the static base,
so the per-workgroup inner shape stays static for any runtime vscale. This
updates the four sites that align distribution to inner tiles:

- root unpack (`setRootConfig(UnPackOp)`),
- root pack (`setRootConfig(PackOp)`), which previously opted out entirely for
  its element-wise behavior but must still align *scalable* dims,
- a non-root pack fused into a root (`adjustTileSizesForRootOp`),
- a root op fusing an unpack (`adjustTileSizesForRootUnPackOp`).

Non-scalable dims and mmt4d/matmul (which distribute on outer dims) are
unchanged. When no `vscale_range` is available the previous static-base +
round-up-to-pow2 behavior is kept.

commit_message:
[Codegen] Forward distribution inner-tile alignment hints in forall tiling

Threads the distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints (set on scalable
`linalg.pack`/`linalg.unpack` ops during lowering-strategy selection) into
`TileAndDistributeToWorkgroupsUsingForall`, via
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn(DistributionTiles)` on both the tiling options and the
consumer-fusion step. With a `Multiple` hint the workgroup tiling folds a
scalable/dynamic inner tile to a clean `tile ceildiv innerTile` division instead
of leaving the pack/unpack untiled.

Adds lit coverage: two scalable pack/unpack cases (hint forwarded and preserved
through tiling) and a dynamic-inner-tile case where the hint is load-bearing —
the pack is only tiled into the forall because the hint asserts the multiple
relationship the driver cannot infer from the IR.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Add vscale_range target field, require it for scalable vec

Introduce a scalable-vector range (`vscale_range`, in vscale units), specified
via `--iree-llvmcpu-vscale-range=<max>` or `=<min,max>`. It is recorded on
`#hal.executable.target` as `vscale_range = [min, max]`.

`getVscaleRange` returns the effective range for a target: a user-specified
range on the config if present, otherwise the target's default
(`getDefaultVscaleRange`, still `{1, 16}` for AArch64 SVE), or nullopt if
neither exists. The LLVM `vscale_range` function attribute is stamped from the
range during serialization (a `+zvlNb` feature raises the min); both the
AArch64 (SVE) and RISC-V (RVV) backends consume it.

A scalable-capable target (SVE or `+v`) with scalable vectorization enabled must
resolve to some range, so strategy selection errors when neither a default nor a
user-specified range exists (e.g. RISC-V `+v` without --iree-llvmcpu-vscale-range).

Existing scalable tests record the range as `[1, 16]`; adds a round-trip test
and an enforcement test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>
name: setup / setup

via `--iree-llvmcpu-vscale-range=<max>` or `=<min,max>`. It is recorded on

range on the config if present, otherwise the target's default
(`getDefaultVscaleRange`, still `{1, 16}` for AArch64 SVE), or nullopt if
neither exists. The LLVM `vscale_range` function attribute is stamped from the
range during serialization (a `+zvlNb` feature raises the min); both the

resolve to some range, so strategy selection errors when neither a default nor a
user-specified range exists (e.g. RISC-V `+v` without --iree-llvmcpu-vscale-range).

Existing scalable tests record the range as `[1, 16]`; adds a round-trip test
and an enforcement test.

commit_message:
[Codegen] Forward distribution inner-tile alignment hints in forall tiling

Threads the distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints (set on scalable
`linalg.pack`/`linalg.unpack` ops during lowering-strategy selection) into
`TileAndDistributeToWorkgroupsUsingForall`, via
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn(DistributionTiles)` on both the tiling options and the
consumer-fusion step. With a `Multiple` hint the workgroup tiling folds a
scalable/dynamic inner tile to a clean `tile ceildiv innerTile` division instead
of leaving the pack/unpack untiled.

Adds lit coverage: two scalable pack/unpack cases (hint forwarded and preserved
through tiling) and a dynamic-inner-tile case where the hint is load-bearing —
the pack is only tiled into the forall because the hint asserts the multiple
relationship the driver cannot infer from the IR.

commit_message:
[Codegen] Forward distribution inner-tile alignment hints in forall tiling

Threads the distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints (set on scalable
`linalg.pack`/`linalg.unpack` ops during lowering-strategy selection) into
`TileAndDistributeToWorkgroupsUsingForall`, via
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn(DistributionTiles)` on both the tiling options and the
consumer-fusion step. With a `Multiple` hint the workgroup tiling folds a
scalable/dynamic inner tile to a clean `tile ceildiv innerTile` division instead
of leaving the pack/unpack untiled.

Adds lit coverage: two scalable pack/unpack cases (hint forwarded and preserved
through tiling) and a dynamic-inner-tile case where the hint is load-bearing —
the pack is only tiled into the forall because the hint asserts the multiple
relationship the driver cannot infer from the IR.

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Align scalable distribution tiles to base * vscaleMax

Distribution tiles for scalable pack/unpack inner dims are aligned to the
largest possible inner tile (`base * vscaleMax`) instead of the static base,
so the per-workgroup inner shape stays static for any runtime vscale. This
updates the four sites that align distribution to inner tiles:

- root unpack (`setRootConfig(UnPackOp)`),
- root pack (`setRootConfig(PackOp)`), which previously opted out entirely for
  its element-wise behavior but must still align *scalable* dims,
- a non-root pack fused into a root (`adjustTileSizesForRootOp`),
- a root op fusing an unpack (`adjustTileSizesForRootUnPackOp`).

Non-scalable dims and mmt4d/matmul (which distribute on outer dims) are
unchanged. When no `vscale_range` is available the previous static-base +
round-up-to-pow2 behavior is kept.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for pack

Extends distribution inner-tile alignment hints to pack ops. A scalable pack's
distribution tile is now aligned to base * vscaleMax, so it is a whole multiple
of the runtime inner tile and gets a `distribution` hint of `Multiple`. This
covers both a pack tiled directly and a pack that consumes an unpack
(`annotateScalablePackConsumerOfUnpack`), which derives its distribution hint
from the unpack's distribution tiles: a match only yields `Multiple` when the
distribution tile is a whole multiple of the pack's largest inner tile, so a
pack whose scalable inner tile differs from its unpack producer's gets no hint.

Packs whose scalable dim is not distributed (e.g. a reduction/broadcast pack)
and mmt4d-fused packs (which distribute on outer dims) are unchanged.

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for unpack

After distribution tiles are aligned to base * vscaleMax (see the preceding
change), a scalable unpack's distribution tile is a whole multiple of the
runtime inner tile for any vscale, so record a `distribution` inner-tile
alignment hint of `Multiple` on it.

A distribution tile is classified as `Multiple` only when it is a whole
multiple of the largest inner tile; mmt4d-fused unpacks (which distribute on
outer dims and are not aligned to inner tiles) therefore get no distribution
hint. Pack distribution hints are added separately.

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for pack

Extends distribution inner-tile alignment hints to pack ops. A scalable pack's
distribution tile is now aligned to base * vscaleMax, so it is a whole multiple
of the runtime inner tile and gets a `distribution` hint of `Multiple`. This
covers both a pack tiled directly and a pack that consumes an unpack
(`annotateScalablePackConsumerOfUnpack`), which derives its distribution hint
from the unpack's distribution tiles: a match only yields `Multiple` when the
distribution tile is a whole multiple of the pack's largest inner tile, so a
pack whose scalable inner tile differs from its unpack producer's gets no hint.

Packs whose scalable dim is not distributed (e.g. a reduction/broadcast pack)
and mmt4d-fused packs (which distribute on outer dims) are unchanged.

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Add vscale_range target field, require it for scalable vec

Introduce a scalable-vector range (`vscale_range`, in vscale units), specified
via `--iree-llvmcpu-vscale-range=<max>` or `=<min,max>`. It is recorded on
`#hal.executable.target` as `vscale_range = [min, max]`.

`getVscaleRange` returns the effective range for a target: a user-specified
range on the config if present, otherwise the target's default
(`getDefaultVscaleRange`, still `{1, 16}` for AArch64 SVE), or nullopt if
neither exists. The LLVM `vscale_range` function attribute is stamped from the
range during serialization (a `+zvlNb` feature raises the min); both the
AArch64 (SVE) and RISC-V (RVV) backends consume it.

A scalable-capable target (SVE or `+v`) with scalable vectorization enabled must
resolve to some range, so strategy selection errors when neither a default nor a
user-specified range exists (e.g. RISC-V `+v` without --iree-llvmcpu-vscale-range).

Existing scalable tests record the range as `[1, 16]`; adds a round-trip test
and an enforcement test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>
name: clang-tidy

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Align scalable distribution tiles to base * vscaleMax

Distribution tiles for scalable pack/unpack inner dims are aligned to the
largest possible inner tile (`base * vscaleMax`) instead of the static base,
so the per-workgroup inner shape stays static for any runtime vscale. This
updates the four sites that align distribution to inner tiles:

- root unpack (`setRootConfig(UnPackOp)`),
- root pack (`setRootConfig(PackOp)`), which previously opted out entirely for
  its element-wise behavior but must still align *scalable* dims,
- a non-root pack fused into a root (`adjustTileSizesForRootOp`),
- a root op fusing an unpack (`adjustTileSizesForRootUnPackOp`).

Non-scalable dims and mmt4d/matmul (which distribute on outer dims) are
unchanged. When no `vscale_range` is available the previous static-base +
round-up-to-pow2 behavior is kept.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>
name: pre-commit

commit_message:
[Codegen] Forward distribution inner-tile alignment hints in forall tiling

Threads the distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints (set on scalable
`linalg.pack`/`linalg.unpack` ops during lowering-strategy selection) into
`TileAndDistributeToWorkgroupsUsingForall`, via
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn(DistributionTiles)` on both the tiling options and the
consumer-fusion step. With a `Multiple` hint the workgroup tiling folds a
scalable/dynamic inner tile to a clean `tile ceildiv innerTile` division instead
of leaving the pack/unpack untiled.

Adds lit coverage: two scalable pack/unpack cases (hint forwarded and preserved
through tiling) and a dynamic-inner-tile case where the hint is load-bearing —
the pack is only tiled into the forall because the hint asserts the multiple
relationship the driver cannot infer from the IR.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

[LLVMCPU] Align scalable distribution tiles to base * vscaleMax

Distribution tiles for scalable pack/unpack inner dims are aligned to the
largest possible inner tile (`base * vscaleMax`) instead of the static base,
so the per-workgroup inner shape stays static for any runtime vscale. This
updates the four sites that align distribution to inner tiles:

- root unpack (`setRootConfig(UnPackOp)`),
- root pack (`setRootConfig(PackOp)`), which previously opted out entirely for
  its element-wise behavior but must still align *scalable* dims,
- a non-root pack fused into a root (`adjustTileSizesForRootOp`),
- a root op fusing an unpack (`adjustTileSizesForRootUnPackOp`).

Non-scalable dims and mmt4d/matmul (which distribute on outer dims) are
unchanged. When no `vscale_range` is available the previous static-base +
round-up-to-pow2 behavior is kept.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for pack

Extends distribution inner-tile alignment hints to pack ops. A scalable pack's
distribution tile is now aligned to base * vscaleMax, so it is a whole multiple
of the runtime inner tile and gets a `distribution` hint of `Multiple`. This
covers both a pack tiled directly and a pack that consumes an unpack
(`annotateScalablePackConsumerOfUnpack`), which derives its distribution hint
from the unpack's distribution tiles: a match only yields `Multiple` when the
distribution tile is a whole multiple of the pack's largest inner tile, so a
pack whose scalable inner tile differs from its unpack producer's gets no hint.

Packs whose scalable dim is not distributed (e.g. a reduction/broadcast pack)
and mmt4d-fused packs (which distribute on outer dims) are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
name: clang-tidy

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for unpack

After distribution tiles are aligned to base * vscaleMax (see the preceding
change), a scalable unpack's distribution tile is a whole multiple of the
runtime inner tile for any vscale, so record a `distribution` inner-tile
alignment hint of `Multiple` on it.

A distribution tile is classified as `Multiple` only when it is a whole
multiple of the largest inner tile; mmt4d-fused unpacks (which distribute on
outer dims and are not aligned to inner tiles) therefore get no distribution
hint. Pack distribution hints are added separately.

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for pack

Extends distribution inner-tile alignment hints to pack ops. A scalable pack's
distribution tile is now aligned to base * vscaleMax, so it is a whole multiple
of the runtime inner tile and gets a `distribution` hint of `Multiple`. This
covers both a pack tiled directly and a pack that consumes an unpack
(`annotateScalablePackConsumerOfUnpack`), which derives its distribution hint
from the unpack's distribution tiles: a match only yields `Multiple` when the
distribution tile is a whole multiple of the pack's largest inner tile, so a
pack whose scalable inner tile differs from its unpack producer's gets no hint.

Packs whose scalable dim is not distributed (e.g. a reduction/broadcast pack)
and mmt4d-fused packs (which distribute on outer dims) are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

distribution tile is now aligned to base * vscaleMax, so it is a whole multiple

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Add vscale_range target field, require it for scalable vec

Introduce a scalable-vector range (`vscale_range`, in vscale units), specified
via `--iree-llvmcpu-vscale-range=<max>` or `=<min,max>`. It is recorded on
`#hal.executable.target` as `vscale_range = [min, max]`.

`getVscaleRange` returns the effective range for a target: a user-specified
range on the config if present, otherwise the target's default
(`getDefaultVscaleRange`, still `{1, 16}` for AArch64 SVE), or nullopt if
neither exists. The LLVM `vscale_range` function attribute is stamped from the
range during serialization (a `+zvlNb` feature raises the min); both the
AArch64 (SVE) and RISC-V (RVV) backends consume it.

A scalable-capable target (SVE or `+v`) with scalable vectorization enabled must
resolve to some range, so strategy selection errors when neither a default nor a
user-specified range exists (e.g. RISC-V `+v` without --iree-llvmcpu-vscale-range).

Existing scalable tests record the range as `[1, 16]`; adds a round-trip test
and an enforcement test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
name: pre-commit

commit_message:
[Codegen] Forward distribution inner-tile alignment hints in forall tiling

Threads the distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints (set on scalable
`linalg.pack`/`linalg.unpack` ops during lowering-strategy selection) into
`TileAndDistributeToWorkgroupsUsingForall`, via
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn(DistributionTiles)` on both the tiling options and the
consumer-fusion step. With a `Multiple` hint the workgroup tiling folds a
scalable/dynamic inner tile to a clean `tile ceildiv innerTile` division instead
of leaving the pack/unpack untiled.

Adds lit coverage: two scalable pack/unpack cases (hint forwarded and preserved
through tiling) and a dynamic-inner-tile case where the hint is load-bearing —
the pack is only tiled into the forall because the hint asserts the multiple
relationship the driver cannot infer from the IR.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Align scalable distribution tiles to base * vscaleMax

Distribution tiles for scalable pack/unpack inner dims are aligned to the
largest possible inner tile (`base * vscaleMax`) instead of the static base,
so the per-workgroup inner shape stays static for any runtime vscale. This
updates the four sites that align distribution to inner tiles:

- root unpack (`setRootConfig(UnPackOp)`),
- root pack (`setRootConfig(PackOp)`), which previously opted out entirely for
  its element-wise behavior but must still align *scalable* dims,
- a non-root pack fused into a root (`adjustTileSizesForRootOp`),
- a root op fusing an unpack (`adjustTileSizesForRootUnPackOp`).

Non-scalable dims and mmt4d/matmul (which distribute on outer dims) are
unchanged. When no `vscale_range` is available the previous static-base +
round-up-to-pow2 behavior is kept.

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for pack

Extends distribution inner-tile alignment hints to pack ops. A scalable pack's
distribution tile is now aligned to base * vscaleMax, so it is a whole multiple
of the runtime inner tile and gets a `distribution` hint of `Multiple`. This
covers both a pack tiled directly and a pack that consumes an unpack
(`annotateScalablePackConsumerOfUnpack`), which derives its distribution hint
from the unpack's distribution tiles: a match only yields `Multiple` when the
distribution tile is a whole multiple of the pack's largest inner tile, so a
pack whose scalable inner tile differs from its unpack producer's gets no hint.

Packs whose scalable dim is not distributed (e.g. a reduction/broadcast pack)
and mmt4d-fused packs (which distribute on outer dims) are unchanged.

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for unpack

After distribution tiles are aligned to base * vscaleMax (see the preceding
change), a scalable unpack's distribution tile is a whole multiple of the
runtime inner tile for any vscale, so record a `distribution` inner-tile
alignment hint of `Multiple` on it.

A distribution tile is classified as `Multiple` only when it is a whole
multiple of the largest inner tile; mmt4d-fused unpacks (which distribute on
outer dims and are not aligned to inner tiles) therefore get no distribution
hint. Pack distribution hints are added separately.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for pack

Extends distribution inner-tile alignment hints to pack ops. A scalable pack's
distribution tile is now aligned to base * vscaleMax, so it is a whole multiple
of the runtime inner tile and gets a `distribution` hint of `Multiple`. This
covers both a pack tiled directly and a pack that consumes an unpack
(`annotateScalablePackConsumerOfUnpack`), which derives its distribution hint
from the unpack's distribution tiles: a match only yields `Multiple` when the
distribution tile is a whole multiple of the pack's largest inner tile, so a
pack whose scalable inner tile differs from its unpack producer's gets no hint.

Packs whose scalable dim is not distributed (e.g. a reduction/broadcast pack)
and mmt4d-fused packs (which distribute on outer dims) are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
name: pre-commit

commit_message:
[Codegen] Forward distribution inner-tile alignment hints in forall tiling

Threads the distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints (set on scalable
`linalg.pack`/`linalg.unpack` ops during lowering-strategy selection) into
`TileAndDistributeToWorkgroupsUsingForall`, via
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn(DistributionTiles)` on both the tiling options and the
consumer-fusion step. With a `Multiple` hint the workgroup tiling folds a
scalable/dynamic inner tile to a clean `tile ceildiv innerTile` division instead
of leaving the pack/unpack untiled.

Adds lit coverage: two scalable pack/unpack cases (hint forwarded and preserved
through tiling) and a dynamic-inner-tile case where the hint is load-bearing —
the pack is only tiled into the forall because the hint asserts the multiple
relationship the driver cannot infer from the IR.

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for unpack

After distribution tiles are aligned to base * vscaleMax (see the preceding
change), a scalable unpack's distribution tile is a whole multiple of the
runtime inner tile for any vscale, so record a `distribution` inner-tile
alignment hint of `Multiple` on it.

A distribution tile is classified as `Multiple` only when it is a whole
multiple of the largest inner tile; mmt4d-fused unpacks (which distribute on
outer dims and are not aligned to inner tiles) therefore get no distribution
hint. Pack distribution hints are added separately.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
name: clang-tidy

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for pack

Extends distribution inner-tile alignment hints to pack ops. A scalable pack's
distribution tile is now aligned to base * vscaleMax, so it is a whole multiple
of the runtime inner tile and gets a `distribution` hint of `Multiple`. This
covers both a pack tiled directly and a pack that consumes an unpack
(`annotateScalablePackConsumerOfUnpack`), which derives its distribution hint
from the unpack's distribution tiles: a match only yields `Multiple` when the
distribution tile is a whole multiple of the pack's largest inner tile, so a
pack whose scalable inner tile differs from its unpack producer's gets no hint.

Packs whose scalable dim is not distributed (e.g. a reduction/broadcast pack)
and mmt4d-fused packs (which distribute on outer dims) are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
name: clang-tidy

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Align scalable distribution tiles to base * vscaleMax

Distribution tiles for scalable pack/unpack inner dims are aligned to the
largest possible inner tile (`base * vscaleMax`) instead of the static base,
so the per-workgroup inner shape stays static for any runtime vscale. This
updates the four sites that align distribution to inner tiles:

- root unpack (`setRootConfig(UnPackOp)`),
- root pack (`setRootConfig(PackOp)`), which previously opted out entirely for
  its element-wise behavior but must still align *scalable* dims,
- a non-root pack fused into a root (`adjustTileSizesForRootOp`),
- a root op fusing an unpack (`adjustTileSizesForRootUnPackOp`).

Non-scalable dims and mmt4d/matmul (which distribute on outer dims) are
unchanged. When no `vscale_range` is available the previous static-base +
round-up-to-pow2 behavior is kept.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
name: clang-tidy

[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for pack

Extends distribution inner-tile alignment hints to pack ops. A scalable pack's
distribution tile is now aligned to base * vscaleMax, so it is a whole multiple
of the runtime inner tile and gets a `distribution` hint of `Multiple`. This
covers both a pack tiled directly and a pack that consumes an unpack
(`annotateScalablePackConsumerOfUnpack`), which derives its distribution hint
from the unpack's distribution tiles: a match only yields `Multiple` when the
distribution tile is a whole multiple of the pack's largest inner tile, so a
pack whose scalable inner tile differs from its unpack producer's gets no hint.

Packs whose scalable dim is not distributed (e.g. a reduction/broadcast pack)
and mmt4d-fused packs (which distribute on outer dims) are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
name: linux_x64_clang_asan

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Align scalable distribution tiles to base * vscaleMax

Distribution tiles for scalable pack/unpack inner dims are aligned to the
largest possible inner tile (`base * vscaleMax`) instead of the static base,
so the per-workgroup inner shape stays static for any runtime vscale. This
updates the four sites that align distribution to inner tiles:

- root unpack (`setRootConfig(UnPackOp)`),
- root pack (`setRootConfig(PackOp)`), which previously opted out entirely for
  its element-wise behavior but must still align *scalable* dims,
- a non-root pack fused into a root (`adjustTileSizesForRootOp`),
- a root op fusing an unpack (`adjustTileSizesForRootUnPackOp`).

Non-scalable dims and mmt4d/matmul (which distribute on outer dims) are
unchanged. When no `vscale_range` is available the previous static-base +
round-up-to-pow2 behavior is kept.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for unpack

After distribution tiles are aligned to base * vscaleMax (see the preceding
change), a scalable unpack's distribution tile is a whole multiple of the
runtime inner tile for any vscale, so record a `distribution` inner-tile
alignment hint of `Multiple` on it.

A distribution tile is classified as `Multiple` only when it is a whole
multiple of the largest inner tile; mmt4d-fused unpacks (which distribute on
outer dims and are not aligned to inner tiles) therefore get no distribution
hint. Pack distribution hints are added separately.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for unpack

After distribution tiles are aligned to base * vscaleMax (see the preceding
change), a scalable unpack's distribution tile is a whole multiple of the
runtime inner tile for any vscale, so record a `distribution` inner-tile
alignment hint of `Multiple` on it.

multiple of the largest inner tile; mmt4d-fused unpacks (which distribute on
outer dims and are not aligned to inner tiles) therefore get no distribution
hint. Pack distribution hints are added separately.

commit_message:
[Codegen] Forward distribution inner-tile alignment hints in forall tiling

Threads the distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints (set on scalable
`linalg.pack`/`linalg.unpack` ops during lowering-strategy selection) into
`TileAndDistributeToWorkgroupsUsingForall`, via
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn(DistributionTiles)` on both the tiling options and the
consumer-fusion step. With a `Multiple` hint the workgroup tiling folds a
scalable/dynamic inner tile to a clean `tile ceildiv innerTile` division instead
of leaving the pack/unpack untiled.

Adds lit coverage: two scalable pack/unpack cases (hint forwarded and preserved
through tiling) and a dynamic-inner-tile case where the hint is load-bearing —
the pack is only tiled into the forall because the hint asserts the multiple
relationship the driver cannot infer from the IR.

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Add vscale_range target field, require it for scalable vec

Introduce a scalable-vector range (`vscale_range`, in vscale units), specified
via `--iree-llvmcpu-vscale-range=<max>` or `=<min,max>`. It is recorded on
`#hal.executable.target` as `vscale_range = [min, max]`.

`getVscaleRange` returns the effective range for a target: a user-specified
range on the config if present, otherwise the target's default
(`getDefaultVscaleRange`, still `{1, 16}` for AArch64 SVE), or nullopt if
neither exists. The LLVM `vscale_range` function attribute is stamped from the
range during serialization (a `+zvlNb` feature raises the min); both the
AArch64 (SVE) and RISC-V (RVV) backends consume it.

A scalable-capable target (SVE or `+v`) with scalable vectorization enabled must
resolve to some range, so strategy selection errors when neither a default nor a
user-specified range exists (e.g. RISC-V `+v` without --iree-llvmcpu-vscale-range).

Existing scalable tests record the range as `[1, 16]`; adds a round-trip test
and an enforcement test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
name: setup / setup

Introduce a scalable-vector range (`vscale_range`, in vscale units), specified
via `--iree-llvmcpu-vscale-range=<max>` or `=<min,max>`. It is recorded on
`#hal.executable.target` as `vscale_range = [min, max]`.

`getVscaleRange` returns the effective range for a target: a user-specified
range on the config if present, otherwise the target's default
(`getDefaultVscaleRange`, still `{1, 16}` for AArch64 SVE), or nullopt if
neither exists. The LLVM `vscale_range` function attribute is stamped from the
range during serialization (a `+zvlNb` feature raises the min); both the
AArch64 (SVE) and RISC-V (RVV) backends consume it.

A scalable-capable target (SVE or `+v`) with scalable vectorization enabled must
resolve to some range, so strategy selection errors when neither a default nor a
user-specified range exists (e.g. RISC-V `+v` without --iree-llvmcpu-vscale-range).

Existing scalable tests record the range as `[1, 16]`; adds a round-trip test
and an enforcement test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
name: runtime_tracing :: windows-2022 :: console

commit_message:
Add bare-metal riscv64 sample and QEMU smoke test to CI

Adds samples/baremetal_riscv64: a single-op inference runner for bare-metal
riscv64 (IREE_PLATFORM_GENERIC, inline HAL) executed on qemu-system-riscv64
(-machine virt, no OS, semihosted I/O), and a pkgci job that builds it and
runs it for both the llvm-cpu (inline-dynamic, embedded-ELF loader) and
vmvx-inline (inline-static) backends.

Design notes:
- samples/simple_embedding's CMake pattern (iree_cc_binary +
  iree_bytecode_module) is the model for the sample, but not its full-HAL
  runtime code: iree_hal_sync_device_create is currently unusable on
  IREE_PLATFORM_GENERIC (device creation eagerly acquires a proactor and no
  generic proactor implementation exists), so the runner uses the inline
  HAL (hal_inline + hal_loader) instead.
- One toolchain/sysroot end to end: xPack riscv-none-elf-gcc, whose newlib

riscv64 (IREE_PLATFORM_GENERIC, inline HAL) executed on qemu-system-riscv64
(-machine virt, no OS, semihosted I/O), and a pkgci job that builds it and
runs it for both the llvm-cpu (inline-dynamic, embedded-ELF loader) and
vmvx-inline (inline-static) backends.

Design notes:
- samples/simple_embedding's CMake pattern (iree_cc_binary +
  iree_bytecode_module) is the model for the sample, but not its full-HAL
  runtime code: iree_hal_sync_device_create is currently unusable on
  IREE_PLATFORM_GENERIC (device creation eagerly acquires a proactor and no
  generic proactor implementation exists), so the runner uses the inline
  HAL (hal_inline + hal_loader) instead.

  is built -mcmodel=medany (QEMU virt RAM starts at 0x80000000, outside
  medlow range) and ships semihost.specs. The riscv-collab LLVM toolchain
  was rejected because its newlib is medlow-built, which would have forced
  linking against a second toolchain's newlib -- not a stable ABI boundary.
- The sample is added with EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL and guarded on a GNU toolchain:
  its link options rely on GCC spec files, so it must not enter the default
  all build of other Generic riscv64 configurations (e.g.
  generic_riscv64.cmake with clang). CI builds it explicitly via
  --target samples/baremetal_riscv64/all.
- The toolchain download is pinned by sha256.

  unsigned char: newlib's ctype macros index a table with the argument and
  GCC's -Werror=char-subscripts rejects plain char there.

commit_message:
Add bare-metal riscv64 sample and QEMU smoke test to CI

Adds samples/baremetal_riscv64: a single-op inference runner for bare-metal
riscv64 (IREE_PLATFORM_GENERIC, inline HAL) executed on qemu-system-riscv64
(-machine virt, no OS, semihosted I/O), and a pkgci job that builds it and
runs it for both the llvm-cpu (inline-dynamic, embedded-ELF loader) and
vmvx-inline (inline-static) backends.

Design notes:
- samples/simple_embedding's CMake pattern (iree_cc_binary +
  iree_bytecode_module) is the model for the sample, but not its full-HAL
  runtime code: iree_hal_sync_device_create is currently unusable on
  IREE_PLATFORM_GENERIC (device creation eagerly acquires a proactor and no
  generic proactor implementation exists), so the runner uses the inline
  HAL (hal_inline + hal_loader) instead.
- One toolchain/sysroot end to end: xPack riscv-none-elf-gcc, whose newlib
  is built -mcmodel=medany (QEMU virt RAM starts at 0x80000000, outside
  medlow range) and ships semihost.specs. The riscv-collab LLVM toolchain
  was rejected because its newlib is medlow-built, which would have forced
  linking against a second toolchain's newlib -- not a stable ABI boundary.
- The sample is added with EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL and guarded on a GNU toolchain:
  its link options rely on GCC spec files, so it must not enter the default
  all build of other Generic riscv64 configurations (e.g.
  generic_riscv64.cmake with clang). CI builds it explicitly via
  --target samples/baremetal_riscv64/all.
- The toolchain download is pinned by sha256.
- Four ctype-macro call sites (string_view.c, regex lexer.c) now cast to
  unsigned char: newlib's ctype macros index a table with the argument and
  GCC's -Werror=char-subscripts rejects plain char there.

commit_message:
Add bare-metal riscv64 sample and QEMU smoke test to CI

Adds samples/baremetal_riscv64: a single-op inference runner for bare-metal
riscv64 (IREE_PLATFORM_GENERIC, inline HAL) executed on qemu-system-riscv64
(-machine virt, no OS, semihosted I/O), and a pkgci job that builds it and
runs it for both the llvm-cpu (inline-dynamic, embedded-ELF loader) and
vmvx-inline (inline-static) backends.

Design notes:
- samples/simple_embedding's CMake pattern (iree_cc_binary +
  iree_bytecode_module) is the model for the sample, but not its full-HAL
  runtime code: iree_hal_sync_device_create is currently unusable on
  IREE_PLATFORM_GENERIC (device creation eagerly acquires a proactor and no
  generic proactor implementation exists), so the runner uses the inline
  HAL (hal_inline + hal_loader) instead.
- One toolchain/sysroot end to end: xPack riscv-none-elf-gcc, whose newlib
  is built -mcmodel=medany (QEMU virt RAM starts at 0x80000000, outside
  medlow range) and ships semihost.specs. The riscv-collab LLVM toolchain
  was rejected because its newlib is medlow-built, which would have forced
  linking against a second toolchain's newlib -- not a stable ABI boundary.
- The sample is added with EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL and guarded on a GNU toolchain:
  its link options rely on GCC spec files, so it must not enter the default
  all build of other Generic riscv64 configurations (e.g.
  generic_riscv64.cmake with clang). CI builds it explicitly via
  --target samples/baremetal_riscv64/all.
- The toolchain download is pinned by sha256.
- Four ctype-macro call sites (string_view.c, regex lexer.c) now cast to
  unsigned char: newlib's ctype macros index a table with the argument and
  GCC's -Werror=char-subscripts rejects plain char there.

Assisted-by: Claude Code
Signed-off-by: Pooja Hemashekar <hemashekar@roofline.ai>
name: setup / setup

(-machine virt, no OS, semihosted I/O), and a pkgci job that builds it and
runs it for both the llvm-cpu (inline-dynamic, embedded-ELF loader) and
vmvx-inline (inline-static) backends.

Design notes:
- samples/simple_embedding's CMake pattern (iree_cc_binary +
  iree_bytecode_module) is the model for the sample, but not its full-HAL
  runtime code: iree_hal_sync_device_create is currently unusable on
  IREE_PLATFORM_GENERIC (device creation eagerly acquires a proactor and no
  generic proactor implementation exists), so the runner uses the inline
  HAL (hal_inline + hal_loader) instead.

  is built -mcmodel=medany (QEMU virt RAM starts at 0x80000000, outside
  medlow range) and ships semihost.specs. The riscv-collab LLVM toolchain
  was rejected because its newlib is medlow-built, which would have forced
  linking against a second toolchain's newlib -- not a stable ABI boundary.
- The sample is added with EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL and guarded on a GNU toolchain:
  its link options rely on GCC spec files, so it must not enter the default
  all build of other Generic riscv64 configurations (e.g.
  generic_riscv64.cmake with clang). CI builds it explicitly via
  --target samples/baremetal_riscv64/all.
- The toolchain download is pinned by sha256.
- Four ctype-macro call sites (string_view.c, regex lexer.c) now cast to
  unsigned char: newlib's ctype macros index a table with the argument and
  GCC's -Werror=char-subscripts rejects plain char there.

commit_message:
[Codegen] Forward distribution inner-tile alignment hints in forall tiling

Threads the distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints (set on scalable
`linalg.pack`/`linalg.unpack` ops during lowering-strategy selection) into
`TileAndDistributeToWorkgroupsUsingForall`, via
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn(DistributionTiles)` on both the tiling options and the
consumer-fusion step. With a `Multiple` hint the workgroup tiling folds a
scalable/dynamic inner tile to a clean `tile ceildiv innerTile` division instead
of leaving the pack/unpack untiled.

Adds lit coverage: two scalable pack/unpack cases (hint forwarded and preserved
through tiling) and a dynamic-inner-tile case where the hint is load-bearing —
the pack is only tiled into the forall because the hint asserts the multiple
relationship the driver cannot infer from the IR.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
name: setup / setup

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for pack

Extends distribution inner-tile alignment hints to pack ops. A scalable pack's
distribution tile is now aligned to base * vscaleMax, so it is a whole multiple
of the runtime inner tile and gets a `distribution` hint of `Multiple`. This
covers both a pack tiled directly and a pack that consumes an unpack
(`annotateScalablePackConsumerOfUnpack`), which derives its distribution hint
from the unpack's distribution tiles: a match only yields `Multiple` when the
distribution tile is a whole multiple of the pack's largest inner tile, so a
pack whose scalable inner tile differs from its unpack producer's gets no hint.

Packs whose scalable dim is not distributed (e.g. a reduction/broadcast pack)
and mmt4d-fused packs (which distribute on outer dims) are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Align scalable distribution tiles to base * vscaleMax

Distribution tiles for scalable pack/unpack inner dims are aligned to the
largest possible inner tile (`base * vscaleMax`) instead of the static base,
so the per-workgroup inner shape stays static for any runtime vscale. This
updates the four sites that align distribution to inner tiles:

- root unpack (`setRootConfig(UnPackOp)`),
- root pack (`setRootConfig(PackOp)`), which previously opted out entirely for
  its element-wise behavior but must still align *scalable* dims,
- a non-root pack fused into a root (`adjustTileSizesForRootOp`),
- a root op fusing an unpack (`adjustTileSizesForRootUnPackOp`).

Non-scalable dims and mmt4d/matmul (which distribute on outer dims) are
unchanged. When no `vscale_range` is available the previous static-base +
round-up-to-pow2 behavior is kept.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
name: clang-tidy

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Add vscale_range target field, require it for scalable vec

Introduce a scalable-vector range (`vscale_range`, in vscale units), specified
via `--iree-llvmcpu-vscale-range=<max>` or `=<min,max>`. It is recorded on
`#hal.executable.target` as `vscale_range = [min, max]`.

`getVscaleRange` returns the effective range for a target: a user-specified
range on the config if present, otherwise the target's default
(`getDefaultVscaleRange`, still `{1, 16}` for AArch64 SVE), or nullopt if
neither exists. The LLVM `vscale_range` function attribute is stamped from the
range during serialization (a `+zvlNb` feature raises the min); both the
AArch64 (SVE) and RISC-V (RVV) backends consume it.

A scalable-capable target (SVE or `+v`) with scalable vectorization enabled must
resolve to some range, so strategy selection errors when neither a default nor a
user-specified range exists (e.g. RISC-V `+v` without --iree-llvmcpu-vscale-range).

Existing scalable tests record the range as `[1, 16]`; adds a round-trip test
and an enforcement test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

[LLVMCPU] Add vscale_range target field, require it for scalable vec

Introduce a scalable-vector range (`vscale_range`, in vscale units), specified
via `--iree-llvmcpu-vscale-range=<max>` or `=<min,max>`. It is recorded on
`#hal.executable.target` as `vscale_range = [min, max]`.

`getVscaleRange` returns the effective range for a target: a user-specified
range on the config if present, otherwise the target's default
(`getDefaultVscaleRange`, still `{1, 16}` for AArch64 SVE), or nullopt if
neither exists. The LLVM `vscale_range` function attribute is stamped from the
range during serialization (a `+zvlNb` feature raises the min); both the
AArch64 (SVE) and RISC-V (RVV) backends consume it.

A scalable-capable target (SVE or `+v`) with scalable vectorization enabled must
resolve to some range, so strategy selection errors when neither a default nor a
user-specified range exists (e.g. RISC-V `+v` without --iree-llvmcpu-vscale-range).

Existing scalable tests record the range as `[1, 16]`; adds a round-trip test
and an enforcement test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
name: linux_x64_clang_debug

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for unpack

After distribution tiles are aligned to base * vscaleMax (see the preceding
change), a scalable unpack's distribution tile is a whole multiple of the
runtime inner tile for any vscale, so record a `distribution` inner-tile
alignment hint of `Multiple` on it.

A distribution tile is classified as `Multiple` only when it is a whole
multiple of the largest inner tile; mmt4d-fused unpacks (which distribute on
outer dims and are not aligned to inner tiles) therefore get no distribution
hint. Pack distribution hints are added separately.

commit_message:
[Codegen] Forward distribution inner-tile alignment hints in forall tiling

Threads the distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints (set on scalable
`linalg.pack`/`linalg.unpack` ops during lowering-strategy selection) into
`TileAndDistributeToWorkgroupsUsingForall`, via
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn(DistributionTiles)` on both the tiling options and the
consumer-fusion step. With a `Multiple` hint the workgroup tiling folds a
scalable/dynamic inner tile to a clean `tile ceildiv innerTile` division instead
of leaving the pack/unpack untiled.

Adds lit coverage: two scalable pack/unpack cases (hint forwarded and preserved
through tiling) and a dynamic-inner-tile case where the hint is load-bearing —
the pack is only tiled into the forall because the hint asserts the multiple
relationship the driver cannot infer from the IR.

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Add vscale_range target field, require it for scalable vec

Add a user-specifiable vscale_range that is recorded on the executable target. This will be used for lowering later on, specifically while setting tile sizes and aligning them to scalable vector sizes.

For targets that support scalable vectorization, specifying this flag is a requirement if scalable vectorization is also enabled. If the target has +zvl*b features and the user specifies a lower bound, the maximum of the two lower bounds will be effective.

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for pack

Extends distribution inner-tile alignment hints to pack ops. A scalable pack's
distribution tile is now aligned to base * vscaleMax, so it is a whole multiple
of the runtime inner tile and gets a `distribution` hint of `Multiple`. This
covers both a pack tiled directly and a pack that consumes an unpack
(`annotateScalablePackConsumerOfUnpack`), which derives its distribution hint
from the unpack's distribution tiles: a match only yields `Multiple` when the
distribution tile is a whole multiple of the pack's largest inner tile, so a
pack whose scalable inner tile differs from its unpack producer's gets no hint.

Packs whose scalable dim is not distributed (e.g. a reduction/broadcast pack)
and mmt4d-fused packs (which distribute on outer dims) are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>
